PCA Imputation for Numeric Matrices

Source: R/pca_imp.R
pca_imp.Rd

Impute missing values in a numeric matrix with regularized or expectation-maximization (EM) PCA imputation. The eigensolver can be LOBPCG, warm-started from the previous eigenblock and search direction.

Usage

pca_imp(
  obj,
  ncp = 2,
  scale = TRUE,
  method = c("regularized", "EM"),
  coeff.ridge = 1,
  row.w = NULL,
  threshold = 1e-06,
  seed = NULL,
  nb.init = 1,
  maxiter = 1000,
  miniter = 5,
  solver = c("auto", "exact", "lobpcg"),
  lobpcg_control = NULL,
  colmax = 0.9,
  post_imp = TRUE,
  clamp = NULL,
  subset = NULL,
  .progress = FALSE
)

Arguments

obj

A double matrix. Samples are in rows and features in columns.

ncp

Integer. Number of principal components used to impute missing values.

scale

Logical. If TRUE, columns are scaled to unit variance.

method

Character. One of "regularized" or "EM". The PCA imputation method.

coeff.ridge

Numeric. The ridge regularization for method = "regularized", ignored otherwise. Values below 1 move toward EM PCA, and values above 1 move toward mean imputation.

row.w

Numeric vector, "n_miss", or NULL. The row weights, normalized to sum to 1: positive values of length nrow(obj), "n_miss" to down-weight rows with more missing values, or NULL for equal weights.

threshold

Numeric. Convergence threshold.

seed

Integer, numeric, or NULL. Random seed for reproducibility. As in missMDA::imputePCA(), initialization i is seeded with seed * (i - 1). So seed = 0 gives every random initialization the same start, and nb.init then yields two distinct solves: the mean initialization and one random one. With nb.init > 1, seed can be at most .Machine$integer.max %/% (nb.init - 1).

nb.init

Integer. Number of initializations. The first is always mean imputation, and the others are random.

maxiter

Integer. Maximum number of iterations.

miniter

Integer. Minimum number of iterations, at most maxiter.

solver

Character. One of "auto", "exact", or "lobpcg". The eigensolver. "auto" uses "exact" for small problems and otherwise runs a short timed probe, picking "lobpcg" only when it is clearly faster. With nb.init > 1, the choice from the first initialization is reused. See the PCA Performance tips section.

lobpcg_control

A list or NULL. LOBPCG control options, from lobpcg_control() or as a plain named list, or NULL for the defaults. Ignored when solver = "exact".

colmax

Numeric scalar between 0 and 1. Columns with a proportion of missing values greater than colmax take no part in the imputation, as described under Column mean fill.

post_imp

Logical. If TRUE, column means replace the missing values that remain after imputation, as described under Column mean fill.

clamp

Numeric vector of length 2 or NULL. The bounds c(lower, upper) for PCA-imputed values, such as c(0, 1) for DNA methylation beta values, or NULL for none. Use -Inf or Inf for a one-sided bound. Observed values are not clamped.

subset

Optional character or integer vector. The columns to impute and return, by name or by number, or NULL for every column. Defaults to NULL.

.progress

Logical. If TRUE, show imputation progress.

Value

A slideimp_results object: a numeric matrix with the rows of obj and the columns that subset selects, with missing values imputed.

Details

pca_imp() reimplements the PCA imputation method from the missMDA package by Francois Husson and Julie Josse, based on Josse and Husson (2016).

A column whose observed values do not vary takes no part in PCA imputation. Column mean fill treats it like a column over colmax, in post_imp and in the mean_filled_cols attribute.

With subset, the result holds only the selected columns, in the order they have in obj. The other columns take part in the imputation as they do without subset. So subset makes the result smaller, not the imputation faster. A name that is not in colnames(obj), or a subset that selects no column, is an error.

PCA Performance tips

Three arguments set the speed: solver, threshold, and scale. Tune these first, then the accuracy arguments ncp and coeff.ridge, on a representative subset.

Exact vs. LOBPCG. "lobpcg" suits large, approximately low-rank matrices with small ncp. "exact" suits small matrices, such as slide_imp() windows, where it is faster. It is also more reliable: it always converges, to eigenvectors exact to machine precision, while LOBPCG stops at the tolerance set in lobpcg_control() and can take many iterations, or reach maxiter, when the eigenvalues around the ncp-th one are close together. The warm start makes each later LOBPCG solve cheap: pca_imp() starts LOBPCG from the previous eigenblock and search direction, so once the imputed values stabilize, each solve takes a few iterations. The gain grows with the number of EM iterations, whatever the rank. solver = "auto", the default, chooses between the two and is a safe start.

Threshold. The default 1e-6 is conservative. 1e-5 is often faster and gives very similar values.

Scale. For columns on a common scale, such as DNA methylation beta values in [0, 1], scale = FALSE can be faster and more accurate.

BLAS. On Windows, the BLAS that ships with R can be slow, and OpenBLAS can replace it.

See Speeding up PCA imputation for the full workflow.

Column mean fill

A column with a proportion of missing values greater than colmax takes no part in the imputation. The method neither uses the column to impute other columns nor imputes it.

With post_imp = TRUE, column means replace the missing values that remain after the method has run. Two kinds of missing value can remain: the missing values of the columns that took no part, and the cells for which the method found no value. Each column mean is the mean of the column's observed values. With post_imp = FALSE, both kinds stay missing.

The result records what the column means replaced, in two attributes:

  • mean_filled_cols: an integer vector with the index, in the result, of each column that took no part and was filled.

  • mean_filled_cells: an integer matrix with the columns row and col, one row for each cell that the method could not impute and that was filled.

Both attributes are empty when no column mean was used. print() reports them when they are not empty.

Missing values and non-finite input

obj must be a double matrix. An integer or logical matrix is rejected, not converted. Convert one with storage.mode(obj) <- "double".

NA and NaN are both treated as missing. The package does not distinguish between them.

Inf and -Inf are rejected on entry, and so is a column with no observed values (every cell NA or NaN). Locate them with which(is.infinite(obj), arr.ind = TRUE) and which(colSums(!is.na(obj)) == 0).

References

Josse J, Husson F (2013). Handling missing values in exploratory multivariate data analysis methods. Journal de la SFdS, 153(2), 79-99.

Josse J, Husson F (2016). missMDA: A Package for Handling Missing Values in Multivariate Data Analysis. Journal of Statistical Software, 70(1), 1-31. doi:10.18637/jss.v070.i01

See also

  • group_imp() to impute within feature groups.

  • mipca() for multiple imputation with PCA.

Examples

set.seed(123)
obj <- sim_mat(10, 10)$input
sum(is.na(obj))
#> [1] 10
obj[1:4, 1:4]
#>          feature1   feature2  feature3  feature4
#> sample1 0.5784798 0.06296727 0.3155309 0.1199980
#> sample2 0.4991812 0.44077231 0.2120510 0.3257524
#> sample3 0.7709271 0.75477764 1.0000000 0.5099311
#> sample4 0.5068375 0.37347042 0.6018860 1.0000000

# Five initializations: the first is mean imputation, the other four are
# random. Select `ncp` with `tune_imp()`.
pca_imp(obj, ncp = 2, nb.init = 5, seed = 123)
#> Method: PCA imputation
#> Dimensions: 10 x 10
#> 
#>          feature1   feature2  feature3  feature4  feature5   feature6
#> sample1 0.5784798 0.06296727 0.3155309 0.1199980 0.1807391 0.31919912
#> sample2 0.4991812 0.44077231 0.2120510 0.3257524 0.1919521 0.14843947
#> sample3 0.7709271 0.75477764 1.0000000 0.5099311 0.6027900 0.75450992
#> sample4 0.5068375 0.37347042 0.6018860 1.0000000 0.5850265 0.08171420
#> sample5 0.4165827 0.42553421 0.6024750 0.7728095 0.2295133 0.08343629
#> sample6 1.0000000 0.93942257 0.9867413 0.5851340 1.0000000 1.00000000
#> # Showing 6 of 10 rows and 6 of 10 columns

# Impute every column, but return only the first three
pca_imp(obj, ncp = 2, subset = 1:3)
#> Method: PCA imputation
#> Dimensions: 10 x 3
#> 
#>          feature1   feature2  feature3
#> sample1 0.5784798 0.06296727 0.3155309
#> sample2 0.4991812 0.44077231 0.2120510
#> sample3 0.7709271 0.75477764 1.0000000
#> sample4 0.5068375 0.37347042 0.6018860
#> sample5 0.4165827 0.42553421 0.6024750
#> sample6 1.0000000 0.93942190 0.9867413
#> # Showing 6 of 10 rows and 3 of 3 columns
